rules.sentence: For example, ETOH-related peripheral neuropathy may be caused by direct nerve injury or by malnutrition.[6]
Multifocal motor neuropathy is an immune-mediated disorder causing asymmetric inflammatory demyelination and remyelination.[7]
HIV-related neuropathies have several distinct categories with variable presentations based on the nerves affected.
For example, mononeuropathy multiplex presents at all stages of HIV infection due to varying etiologies.

Autonomic neuropathy may also occur in the HIV patient when there is damage to the nerves responsible for functions that regulate autonomic activities such as blood pressure, heart rate, or bowel and bladder emptying.[8]
It is important to note that EDX can only test Type I fibers and cannot detect small fiber neuropathies.
Common disorders that produce small fiber neuropathies are diabetes, amyloidosis, and HIV.[9][10]

When a patient describes symptoms such as paresthesias, pain, or weakness in more than 1 extremity, which cannot be explained by a focal mononeuropathy, such as nerve entrapment neuropathy, the clinician may turn to EDX to identify whether a peripheral neuropathy may be present.
The EDX may also help narrow the differential diagnosis based on the disease’s common electrodiagnostic features.[10][11]
